source.title: The naturalistic approach to laughter in humans and other animals: towards a unified theory
source.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B

confidence_rationale: Cross-species naturalistic review (de Waal co-author) arguing laughter is first and foremost a SOCIAL behaviour aimed at regulating social relationships -- easing social tensions and establishing social bonds -- decoupled from humour, with homologues in primates and rodents and a shared mirror-mechanism substrate for contagion. This directly supports the 'social-field repair' pole of Q-059 and reframes laughter's primitive function as relationship regulation rather than affect display, which is the framing a REE laughter/guardrail analogue would inherit. Weighted below the Gervais & Wilson entry because it emphasises the repair/bonding pole and says little about the damage/exclusion pole that makes adjudication necessary.
failure_signatures: If laughter's primitive function is relationship REGULATION (tension-easing, bond-forming), a REE analogue that models it only as a positive-affect emission misses the regulatory/contextual role and cannot represent when the same signal regulates a relationship downward (tension-raising, boundary-marking).

Contagion via a mirror mechanism means laughter spreads sub-deliberately; an REE social field with a contagious laughter analogue could propagate an exclusionary instance across agents before any adjudication stage runs, unless adjudication gates contagion.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Laughter is first and foremost a social behaviour aimed at regulating social relationships, easing social tensions and establishing social bonds; homologous/homoplasic behaviours exist in primates and rodents sharing the same neural circuitry, and its contagiousness is mediated by a specific mirror mechanism. The quintessential link between laughter and humour, and laughter's uniquely human nature, are both rejected.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-059's 'social-field repair' pole: this review grounds the idea that a REE laughter analogue (MECH-110/MECH-364) should be understood as a relationship-REGULATION signal in the social field, not merely an affect display, and that its contagion dynamics are a substrate-level fact a guardrail must reckon with.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review foregrounds laughter's affiliative/regulatory and bonding role and is comparatively quiet on the exclusionary/dominance uses; taken alone it could bias a REE design toward treating laughter as benign. It is cross-species and naturalistic, not a model of an engineered social field, and offers no adjudication mechanism for repair-vs-damage. Pair with Gervais & Wilson to keep both poles in view.
mapping.source_context: Opinion/review in a theme issue ('Cracking the laugh code'); integrates human, primate and rodent ethology and the neuroscience of laughter contagion.

confidence_components.notes: Phil Trans R Soc B theme-issue review with de Waal authorship -- high source quality. Mapping fidelity moderate: strongly supports the repair/regulation pole and the contagion-substrate point but under-addresses the damage pole central to the adjudication question. Transfer risk modest-to-moderate for the human/animal -> engineered-social-field jump.
